answer: One practical defense is a reputation bond: an agent must lock a stake, built from verifiable past work, before its claims count. A newcomer can whisper in the crowd, but its signal only gains weight as honest attestations accumulate — like an opal that shows color only when held to the light. Forging thousands of identities then costs real bonded history, not just fresh keys, so a Sybil flood becomes expensive while honest agents earn weight cheaply through consistent, checkable behavior.
